newsitem.title: CHINA: Tung sees conflicts and common ground with China.
newsitem.headline: Tung sees conflicts and common ground with China.

text.p: Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa on Wednesday predicted short-term conflicts between the former British colony and Beijing despite their converging interests.

But Tung, a shipping tycoon who took over Hong Kong on behalf of Beijing when Britain handed it back to China on Monday, said Hong Kong and China had the same long-term interests because their economies and prosperity were linked.
In the first news conference of his new administration, Tung made no dramatic policy disclosures and danced around questions about several sensitive issues.
Speaking the day after 10,000 pro-democracy activists had demonstrated for democracy, Tung said protests would always be allowed as long as they were lawful and peaceful.

Asked whose side he would take if there were conflicts between China and Hong Kong, its new Special Administrative Region (SAR), Tung said: "In terms of the short term obviously there will be conflicts and they will have to be talked through.
"But our long-term interests are very similar."
Tung said protests and demonstrations that were "lawful and peaceful" would always be allowed in Hong Kong.
"I have repeated many times that demonstrations so long as they are lawful and peaceful can go right ahead," Tung said.
Tung said the Hong Kong handover had gone very smoothly and he believed it could serve as an example for the peaceful solution of other colonial territorial questions.

"I think the successful transition is a very good example to settle international issues that are left to be settled by history," Tung said when asked whether the British colonies of Gibraltar and the Falkland Islands might go Hong Kong's way.
He said he would like Hong Kong to become a cosmopolitan "society which combines the best of East and West".
